columns.question: Under which storage conditions are the stability samples stored?
columns.instructions: Give every condition this study uses (long-term, intermediate, accelerated, in-use), with temperature and humidity tolerances and any orientation or container note. Leave out conditions mentioned only as background.

columns.question: At which timepoints are samples pulled and tested?
columns.instructions: One item per storage condition, e.g. "Long-term: 0, 3, 6, 9, 12 months". Use the schedule in this version of the protocol, including every timepoint.

columns.question: What are the shelf-life acceptance criteria for the stability tests?
columns.instructions: List each test with its limit, e.g. "Assay: 95.0-105.0% of label claim". Use the limits this protocol states for its own stability testing, not limits it quotes from other documents.

columns.question: Which deviations from the protocol have been recorded?
columns.instructions: Include deviations mentioned anywhere, including appendices. One item per deviation: its ID and a short description. If the document states that no deviations have occurred, return an empty list [] (not an item saying so) and cite that statement. If the document does not address deviations at all, set found to false.

columns.question: How does the protocol justify its bracketing or matrixing design, or its decision not to use one?
columns.instructions: Summarize the stated rationale: which strengths, fills or packs are tested and why they represent the others, or why a reduced design is not used. Count only what the document explicitly says about bracketing, matrixing or a reduced design; do not infer a rationale from the scope or from which batches or packs happen to be tested. If the document never addresses bracketing or matrixing, set found to false.

columns.question: What post-approval stability commitment does the protocol make?
columns.instructions: State which batches are committed, at which condition, for how long, and how results are reported. Count only a commitment the document explicitly makes to a health authority or in the registration (e.g. "the applicant commits to..."). An ongoing or annual stability programme that the protocol simply runs is not a commitment unless the document calls it one. If the protocol makes no post-approval commitment, set found to false.
